items.summary: Fortinet FortiMail zero-day (advisory FG-IR-26-175) combining path traversal with NULL-byte neutralization, letting unauthenticated attackers write arbitrary files to the FortiMail OS via crafted requests to the management interface. Actively exploited in the wild; CISA added it to KEV on Oct 1, and at publication no patch existed — only interim workarounds.

UTMStack's incident-command WebSocket handler (/command/{hostname} STOMP destination) applies no role check or command allowlist, so any authenticated user can send arbitrary OS commands via gRPC to every connected agent — which typically run as root/SYSTEM. Disclosed Oct 2 alongside six other UTMStack flaws; fixed in 11.2.16.

Sandbox escape in GitLab's self-hosted AI Gateway: a logged-in user with Duo Agent Platform access can craft a flow configuration that escapes the Jinja2 prompt-template sandbox and executes arbitrary commands on the gateway host (server-side, before any LLM invocation). Affects 18.1.6–19.4.0; operators must update the Gateway image itself to 19.2.4, 19.3.2 or 19.4.1.

Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway zero-day enabling unauthenticated remote code execution in default configuration, part of a cluster of eight actively attacked vulnerabilities. Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant report custom WHIPSHOT web shells and SLAPSHOT tunnelers being used for persistent access against targets in Europe and North America.

ConvertX before 0.19.0 passes Calibre recipe files straight to the ebook-convert binary without blocking them, so executable code in a .recipe or .downloaded_recipe file runs on the host (CWE-829). Disclosed Oct 3; upgrade to 0.19.0 or later.
